To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the swelling assay for putative aquaporins is not as simple a process as has been assumed; but that the traditional interpretation is probably not seriously in error.

the swelling assay is a valid method for the detection of aquaporin-like activity; that it should be valid even when the elastic modulus is not vanishingly small; and that it should be possible to model the assay with reasonable accuracy by a Stefan-like moving boundary problem.

the swelling assay for water transporters is well described by a moving boundary model of a spherical cell in hypotonic medium, and that the time course of the swelling is not well approximated by the exponential function used in traditional interpretation of experimental data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical modelling of aquaporin expression assays.
the development of an analytical model of the swelling assay for the detection of aquaporin-like water transporters, which is the standard method of assuring the function of such proteins.
the modelling and simulation of a swelling assay for water permeability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the swelling assay for the expression of aquaporins can be modelled by the perfect-mix assumption and is likely to give results which are not seriously affected by this assumption, but that the perfect-mix simplification is not valid in all cases.
, although the standard interpretation of swelling assays is probably correct in its essentials, the details of the interpretation are not well understood.

the standard interpretation of the swelling assay should not be seriously affected by the assumptions of perfect mixing, diffusive equilibrium, and vanishingly small membrane modulus, and that it is probably safe to assume that these conditions hold in the standard assay.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the standard assay for aquaporins is likely to be valid, although it should be possible in some cases to obtain more accurate results by more careful modelling.
, while the standard interpretation of aquaporin expression assays should be valid in many cases, the use of a simple exponential model may lead to under-estimates of aquaporin permeability.
the standard method of assuring aquaporin-like entities should be valid, but that the interpretation of the swelling behavior should be done with caution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the traditional interpretation of swelling assays is valid in most circumstances.

, in spite of the apparent complexity of the swelling assay, its interpretation should be straightforward if the cell is not too large, if diffusive movement of the osmolyte is not too slow and if the cell membrane is not too strong.
, in spite of the complexity of the problem, a simple linear model should be adequate to describe swelling in most cases.
